description: Agreement between the engine's skill order in generated paths and the majority order observed in real learner sequences, per source. Computed by pipeline/evaluate/sequencing_agreement.py; nothing trained.

method.agreement: the engine's order matches the observed majority direction
method.confound: the engine's order is partly derived from the authored prerequisite graph, and the authored edges are what the sources were already checked against in the agreement report; the unrelated split is the least confounded view and the authored-edge split the most
method.corpus: 5 fixture learners + 15 goal templates x 3 canonical profiles (empty, partial, time-poor) = 50 generated paths
method.observed: a source observed the pair with n >= 20 (the file's confirm floor) and a strict majority; majority direction = support > reverse
method.pair: ordered pair (A, B) of taught skills where A's first teaching item precedes B's first teaching item in path order; assessments do not teach, and an item teaches a skill only above the level the learner already holds; ties (same item) are not pairs
method.relation: authored-edge: A -> B is an authored prerequisite edge; graph-derived: A is a transitive prerequisite of B through path-driving edges (the engine's order follows the graph); graph-inverted: the graph says B before A yet the engine taught A first (a phase project covering a skill before its prerequisite course, or a cycle-broken soft edge) — an engine finding, not a learner-order one; unrelated: no graph relation either way (the order came from scoring and phasing, not from a prerequisite claim)
